questions.stem: According to the passage, what does Suzanne Meyer say students need to learn to do in order to develop critical thinking skills?
options: Memorize as many facts as possible
Collect information, evaluate it, and apply it to a new context
Only ask questions that teachers assign
Avoid asking questions in class
questions.evidence: students need to learn how to collect information, and then evaluate the information and apply it to a new context
questions.explanation_ko: 학생들은 정보를 모으고 평가한 뒤 새로운 맥락에 적용하는 법을 배워야 한다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from Meyer's observation that students are less creative with questions when teachers assign exactly which ones to answer?
options: Students are more likely to think creatively when they create their own questions rather than answer assigned ones.
Teachers should always assign the exact questions students must answer.
Critical thinking cannot be taught through question-asking.
Creative questions are less useful than assigned questions for learning.
questions.evidence: when teachers tell students which questions to answer, students are less likely to be creative about the types of questions that they ask
questions.explanation_ko: 교사가 답할 질문을 지정해 주면 학생들이 창의적으로 질문을 만들 가능성이 줄어든다는 내용에서, 스스로 질문을 만드는 것이 창의성에 더 도움이 됨을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author suggest students design questions that move from "concrete" to "abstract"?
options: To provide a strategy for building critical thinking step by step, starting with specific details before moving to bigger ideas
To make English grammar easier to memorize
To help students avoid asking questions altogether
To test students on vocabulary words only
questions.evidence: use question-asking patterns that start with concrete questions and move to abstract questions
questions.explanation_ko: 이 전략은 구체적인 것에서 추상적인 것으로 나아가며 비판적 사고를 단계적으로 기르기 위한 방법을 제시하기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "inquiry" mean in "get students actively engaged in inquiry"?
options: silence
the act of asking questions to gather information
memorization
competition
questions.evidence: get students actively engaged in inquiry
questions.explanation_ko: inquiry는 정보를 모으기 위해 질문하는 행위를 뜻합니다.

questions.stem: Which choice best restates: "Question-asking activities help students to become better language learners."
options: Practicing how to ask questions can make students more effective at learning a language.
Only teachers should ask questions in the classroom.
Students must avoid asking too many questions to learn a language well.
Learning a language does not require asking questions.
questions.evidence: Question-asking activities help students to become better language learners.
questions.explanation_ko: 질문하기 활동이 학생들을 더 나은 언어 학습자로 만드는 데 도움이 된다는 문장을 가장 가깝게 재진술한 선택지는 첫 번째입니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 우리는 학생들이 초급 단계부터 전문적·대학 수준에 가까운 단계에 이르기까지 적극적으로 탐구에 참여하게 해야 합니다.
질문하기를 한번 시도해 보시고, 어떻게 되었는지 알려 주세요!
질문하기 활동은 학생들이 더 나은 언어 학습자가 되도록 돕는다.
교사가 답할 질문을 지정해 주면 학생들은 스스로 질문을 만드는 데 있어 창의적일 가능성이 더 낮아진다.

key_points: Suzanne Meyer says many students need to develop critical thinking skills, which involve collecting, evaluating, and applying information.
Teaching students to ask creative questions is one way to build critical thinking and helps them become better language learners.
One strategy is to design a sequence of questions that moves from concrete details to more abstract ideas.
Meyer notes that students are less creative in their questioning when teachers assign the exact questions to answer, so she encourages learners to write their own questions.
main_idea: Suzanne Meyer explains that teaching English learners to ask their own questions, moving from concrete to abstract, helps them build critical thinking skills.
restate_sentence: One way to develop critical thinking skills, Meyer says, is to teach students to be creative about the types of questions that they ask.
